clue.text: Wise man immersed in drink rolling over to see stars

indicators.note: rolling over turns the whole assembly the other way round, so it is read backwards
one piece immersed in another sits inside it

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A sage, slumped in his cups and rolling over, sees stars after drinking too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling over' reverses the whole drink-with-sage assembly, so the drunk sage's tumble is the reversal; 'stars' is the constellation, not celebrities or a dizzy head.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a constellation, the winged horse of the northern sky, so a group of stars.

clue.text: Playwright beginning with page that expresses contempt

indicators.note: the playwright begins with the page, so that letter goes in front

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw, the Irish dramatist

explanation.surface: A dramatist starts a page that is scornful in tone.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of scorn or impatience, a word uttered to show disdain.

clue.text: Managed to break into holiday home — it's very hard

indicators.note: the word for managed breaks into, so sits inside, the holiday home

parts.note: a gite is a French holiday cottage
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Someone managed a break-in at a holiday cottage, and found it a tough job.
explanation.definitionFit: An igneous rock famous for its toughness, used for kerbs and worktops.

clue.text: Little nonentity not in clique

indicators.note: not in means the word in is removed from the longer word

parts.note: an insect is a small creature, and figuratively an insignificant person

explanation.surface: A small, insignificant person is excluded from the in-crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a small exclusive group, close in sense to a clique or faction.

clue.text: Billy Graham type is "OT/NT-basher", put unfairly

indicators.note: something put unfairly is misrepresented, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An American evangelist is accused, unfairly, of bashing both Testaments of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: OT and NT are the Old and New Testaments; the fodder is IS, OTNTBASHER and PUT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy Graham was the best-known preacher of this large American evangelical denomination.

clue.text: Inspired Democrat lagging behind popular Italian dictator?

indicators.note: the Democrat lags behind, so it comes after the other pieces

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Il Duce was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: A Democrat trails in the polls behind a well-liked strongman, wondering whether that was inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Induced and inspired both mean brought about or prompted, as in a feeling caused by something.

clue.text: Accident insurer finally sorted out, giving apology for mistake

indicators.note: sorted out suggests the letters are rearranged into new order
finally picks the closing letter of the word insurer

explanation.surface: An insurer finally settles an accident claim, issuing an apology for its error.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is ACCIDENT, R (last of insurer) and SORTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock phrase of admission: someone saying it concedes that they got something wrong.

clue.text: I mend TV set that's broken for selling off

indicators.note: a broken set has its parts in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A repairer fixes a broken television so it can be sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Divestment is disposing of assets, typically by sale, which is selling off.

clue.text: City girl keeping a date that brings new life

indicators.note: one word keeping another holds it inside

parts.note: Cora is a girl's name
DOB, date of birth, is the date on which a new life arrives

explanation.surface: A young woman from the city goes on a date and finds it revitalising.
explanation.walkthrough: DOB is the common form-filling abbreviation for date of birth.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic city in Andalusia, Spain, famous for its great mosque-cathedral.

clue.text: Examine and discredit one form of therapy

parts.note: to diss is to disrespect or run down
ECT, electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.surface: A sceptic examines a type of treatment and rubbishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissect is to analyse something closely, piece by piece.

clue.text: People on staff matter to boss

indicators.note: matter is added to the boss, joined on after it

parts.note: the head is the boss
to count is to matter, to be significant

explanation.surface: Employees are important to their manager.
explanation.definitionFit: The number of employees an organisation has, its total staff.

clue.text: A classical man to you and me represents something harmful

parts.note: vir is Latin for man
us means you and me

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman, to ordinary folk, is a menace.
explanation.definitionFit: A virus is an infectious agent, a damaging thing in a body or a computer.

clue.text: Archbishop's envoy reported delay

indicators.note: reported means as said aloud, so the name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Terry Waite was the Archbishop of Canterbury's special envoy, held hostage in Lebanon

explanation.surface: News of a postponement involving a church emissary.
explanation.walkthrough: Terry Waite, the Church of England envoy taken hostage in Beirut in 1987, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To wait is to hold back, and a wait is a period of hold-up.

clue.text: Dodgy shiner not ultimately genuine

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable, so these letters are untrustworthy in their order
ultimately picks the last letter of genuine

explanation.surface: A sparkly stone turns out to be fake.
explanation.walkthrough: SHINER and NOT are shuffled, then E (last of genuine) is added; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhinestone is an imitation diamond, a glittering stone that is not real.

clue.text: Kind to preside over slightly twisted board

indicators.note: a slight twist shifts just one letter to a new spot
in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it

parts.note: to chair is to preside over a meeting
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A generous person presides over a slightly warped committee.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAIR over TABLE gives CHAIRTABLE; 'slightly twisted' moves the I one place later.
explanation.definitionFit: Being charitable is being generous and benevolent toward others, so kind.

clue.text: Endure losing a sheep

indicators.note: losing a means that letter drops out

parts.note: to weather a storm is to endure it

explanation.surface: A sheep endures loss.
explanation.definitionFit: A wether is a castrated ram, a male sheep.

clue.text: Firm's contract

definitions.meaning: solid and dense, as firm packed earth
an agreement, a treaty or pact between parties

explanation.surface: A business agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Compact means both solid and close-packed, and a formal pact between parties.

clue.text: North African countries suffering big harm

indicators.note: suffering harm puts the letters in a damaged order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nations of North Africa enduring great damage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maghrib (Maghreb) is the region of northwest Africa: Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia and Libya.

clue.text: Put illiterately, Queen and I go walkabout

indicators.note: said ungrammatically, the Queen and I comes out with me in place of I, placed first

parts.note: me stands for I in illiterate speech
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Speaking ungrammatically, a royal says she and the monarch are off on a tour.
explanation.walkthrough: The illiterate version of 'the Queen and I' is 'me and the Queen', giving ME AND ER. A royal walkabout is a stroll to meet crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wander aimlessly, much like going walkabout.

clue.text: Boleyn and husband, say, set up in hellish situation

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: Anne Boleyn, Henry VIII's second wife
eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: Anne Boleyn and Henry VIII set up home in a hellish place.
explanation.definitionFit: Gehenna is a biblical name for hell, or any place of torment.

clue.text: Row created by the French to fester

parts.note: a rank is a row, as of soldiers or taxis
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An argument started by the French is left to fester.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to cause lasting resentment, festering in the mind.

clue.text: A place bathed in light? Not in the winter

definitions.text: A place bathed in light? Not in the winter

parts.words: A place bathed in light? Not in the winter
parts.note: a lap is where you sit something, and land beyond the Arctic Circle gets the midnight sun in summer but endless dark in winter

explanation.surface: A sunny spot that turns dark come winter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic region of northern Scandinavia sees the midnight sun in summer and polar night in winter.

clue.text: Dryden character in a note on work he left

parts.note: C is a musical note
something in is popular, a hit
op, opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A literary figure appears in a musical piece he walked out on.
explanation.walkthrough: Absalom and Achitophel is Dryden's 1681 political satire.
explanation.definitionFit: Achitophel is the scheming counsellor in Dryden's satirical poem, standing for the Earl of Shaftesbury.

clue.text: Note put about in the morning conveys unwanted message

indicators.note: put about means turned around, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is a note added to a letter
am means in the morning

explanation.surface: A note sent round first thing contains an unwelcome message.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is junk email, messages nobody asked for.

clue.text: Morning — chief time to get stuck in

indicators.note: time getting stuck in means it is lodged inside another word

parts.note: main means chief

explanation.surface: A boss urges an early start: time to get going.
explanation.definitionFit: Matin, as in matins, relates to the morning, and is French for that time of day.

clue.text: Inadequacy of computer being set up is concerning

indicators.note: in a down clue being set up means written upwards, so read backwards
an inadequate version falls short, so the last letter is missing

parts.note: ERNIE is the British computer that picks Premium Bond winners

explanation.surface: The failure of a computer installation is worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE picks winning numbers for Premium Bonds, a UK government savings lottery; cut to ERNI and turned up, it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In re is a Latin phrase meaning in the matter of, or about.

clue.text: Star inside nebula not entirely detectable

indicators.note: only part of the words can be seen, so the answer lies hidden within them

explanation.surface: A star within a gas cloud can barely be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' looks like the hidden-word signal, but it is part of the text: the answer straddles insiDE NEBula.
explanation.definitionFit: Deneb is the brightest star in the constellation Cygnus.

clue.text: Home worker engaging nurse and manager

indicators.note: engaging means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: in means at home
the ant is the crossword's usual worker insect
to tend is to nurse

explanation.surface: A domestic employee takes on a nurse and an administrator.
explanation.definitionFit: An intendant is a superintendent or administrator, an official in charge.

clue.text: Name of London street hiding a chemical

indicators.note: hiding means holding something within

parts.note: Regent Street is a major shopping street in London's West End

explanation.surface: A London street name conceals a chemical substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance used to bring about a chemical reaction.

clue.text: Briefly arrange private office in German city

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to dress is to arrange, as a window display
a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: A quick tidy-up of a study in a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Dresden is the capital of Saxony in eastern Germany.
